fields: Do Not Start With This When

rows.Main Input: target-sample measured submicron or high-density spatial transcriptomics data
rows.Main Use in This Topic: segmentation-free analysis of already fine-geometry spatial transcriptomics for factor-level representation
rows.Main Output: segmentation-free fine-scale spatial factor and tissue-feature maps
rows.Key Difference: Represents measured high-density/submicron spatial signal without requiring segmentation; it is not a spot-to-subspot reconstruction method.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence: PubMed verifies PMID 39266749 and DOI 10.1038/s41592-024-02415-2 for the Nature Methods FICTURE paper, and Layer 1 records the primary GitHub link. Layer 2 synthesis: closest alternatives, resource burden, and topic fit as a super-resolution branch are interpretive; code access does not imply execution readiness.
rows.Best First Choice When: Consider when the task starts from measured submicron or high-density spatial transcriptomics and asks for segmentation-free fine-scale representation.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: Consider other Super-resolution rows when the task is low-resolution spot-to-subspot reconstruction or histology-guided generated high-density expression.
rows.Signal-risk Caveat: FICTURE operates on measured fine-geometry spatial signal; do not present it as generating pseudo-cell expression or reconstructing unmeasured molecules.

rows.Main Input: target-sample spot-based spatial transcriptomics with matched histology
rows.Main Use in This Topic: histology-guided inference of super-resolution tissue architecture
rows.Main Output: super-resolved tissue architecture and inferred fine-resolution expression map
rows.Key Difference: Uses hierarchical image features with ST-histology integration, emphasizing tissue architecture rather than only expression-grid interpolation.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence: PubMed verifies PMID 38168986 and DOI 10.1038/s41587-023-02019-9, and the 2026-05-04 targeted metadata/code check records the primary GitHub trace. Layer 2 synthesis: comparator and scale cues are not independent benchmark results; code access does not imply execution readiness.
rows.Best First Choice When: Consider when the task has a target-sample measured spatial expression anchor and asks for finer-geometry reconstruction of that same sample signal.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: Consider when no matched image is available or the desired output is segmentation-free factor maps from already submicron data.
rows.Signal-risk Caveat: Histology-guided inference can overfit morphology and may under-represent molecular programs that are weakly visible in the image. Outputs are inferred reconstructions anchored to target-sample measured spatial data; pseudo-cell, single-cell-resolution, high-density, or cell-level outputs are not direct molecule-level single-cell measurements.

rows.Main Input: target-sample spot-based ST, spatial coordinates, and histology image
rows.Main Use in This Topic: single-cell-resolution spatial gene-expression inference from fused expression, location, and image signals
rows.Key Difference: Combines image representation and spatial graph convolution for single-cell-resolution expression inference rather than pseudo-single-cell whole-transcriptome reconstruction across an entire section.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence: PubMed verifies PMID 39656774 and DOI 10.1093/bib/bbae630, and the 2026-05-04 targeted metadata/code check records the primary GitHub trace. Layer 2 synthesis: resource and comparison cues are not independent benchmark results; code access does not imply execution readiness.
rows.Best First Choice When: Consider when the task has a target-sample measured spatial expression anchor and asks for finer-geometry reconstruction of that same sample signal.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: Consider when a simpler histology-to-expression method better matches the task or when the task is pseudo-single-cell whole-section reconstruction rather than graph/image expression inference.
rows.Signal-risk Caveat: Graph and image fusion can propagate image-driven or neighborhood-driven assumptions into expression estimates; validation should not rely only on visual plausibility. rows.Main Input: target-sample section-level spatial transcriptomics with image/context features
rows.Main Use in This Topic: single-cell spatial whole-transcriptome reconstruction across an entire tissue section
rows.Key Difference: Targets section-wide single-cell spatial whole-transcriptome reconstruction, making whole-section coverage a stronger cue than tumor-specific or local super-resolution use.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence: PubMed verifies PMID 40074951 and DOI 10.1038/s41592-025-02622-5, and Layer 1 records the primary GitHub link. Layer 2 synthesis: scale and branch placement are interpreted from the whole-section reconstruction claim, not from a cross-method benchmark; code access does not imply execution readiness.
rows.Best First Choice When: Consider when the task has a target-sample measured spatial expression anchor and asks for finer-geometry reconstruction of that same sample signal.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: Consider when the target is submicron factorization, high-density assay generation, or a tumor-ecosystem-specific super-resolution workflow.
rows.Signal-risk Caveat: Pseudo-single-cell reconstruction can create a false sense of measured cellular certainty; downstream claims should separate inferred cells from assayed molecules. Outputs are inferred reconstructions anchored to target-sample measured spatial data; pseudo-cell, single-cell-resolution, high-density, or cell-level outputs are not direct molecule-level single-cell measurements.

rows.Method Family: Reference- and histology-guided continuous whole-slide reconstruction
rows.Main Input: target-sample low-resolution spatial transcriptomics with matched histology and a matched scRNA-seq reference
rows.Main Use in This Topic: continuous whole-slide single-cell reconstruction anchored to target-sample measured spatial transcriptomics
rows.Main Output: continuous whole-slide single-cell-resolution spatial transcriptome map
rows.Key Difference: Uses a matched scRNA-seq reference plus histology to reconstruct a continuous whole-slide single-cell map from low-resolution ST rather than relying only on image fusion or pseudo-cell reconstruction within the measured section.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence: Nature Computational Science verifies DOI 10.1038/s43588-025-00938-y and the 2026-01-06 publication date for the PanoSpace paper, and code availability points to the public GitHub repository. Layer 2 synthesis: branch placement under Super-resolution rather than Cell Type Inference follows the measured-anchor output object, not runtime validation.
rows.Best First Choice When: Consider when low-resolution target-sample spatial transcriptomics, matched histology, and a matched scRNA-seq reference are available and the task asks for continuous whole-slide single-cell reconstruction of the same sample signal.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: Consider other Super-resolution or Cell Type Inference rows when the task is plain cell-type placement, spot-level deconvolution, or histology-guided reconstruction without a matched scRNA-seq reference.
rows.Cellular Reconstruction Mode: reference- and histology-guided continuous whole-slide reconstruction
rows.Signal-risk Caveat: Reference- and histology-guided continuous reconstruction can amplify reference mismatch, morphology-driven hallucination, or overconfident cell-level continuity; outputs remain inferred reconstructions anchored to target-sample measured spatial data, not direct molecule-level single-cell measurements.
